The xDrip+ server listens on 127.0.0.1:17580, like xDrip+ itself, so Garmin faces and data fields made for xDrip+ read it. The Nightscout API is plain HTTP: share it only on networks you trust.

In range is %1$d–%2$d mg/dL; very good (%1$d–%3$d) is the part of it where people without diabetes spend most of the day. Very low and very high are the levels of the LibreView report. Extremely high only changes the colour of the line and the number; the report counts it as very high. The ranges colour the number, the line, the status bar and the time in range everywhere.
Dashed lines across the graph at the levels you pick, besides the range limits. Small graphs space the vertical lines further apart; the times under the graph stay when they\'re off.
Each widget can have its own window: touch and hold it, then tap Reconfigure.
Ring order, clockwise from the top

Each slot is a time-in-range ring or a number from your doctor\'s report: GMI, average glucose or variability (CV), with a green arc when its goal is met. Slots that don\'t fit are hidden, the last one first. A slot needs data for at least a quarter of its window. Last treatment shows your latest rapid insulin (for 4 h, ahead of carbs while its alert pause lasts) or carbs (up to 3 h, less for small amounts): the amount, the time since, and a ring for the time left before alerts come back. It takes the second slot\'s place when there\'s room for only two.

Close treatments share one label, like 4u · 40g 1h 4m. Hidden amounts leave it, and the time shows once, since the newest treatment that shows its time. Every graph uses these: the app, the notification, the widgets and the lock screen.

The sensor\'s time left goes at the start of the time row, under the % of time in range (a card without a graph shows just the number). The warm-up and \"Sensor ended\" show either way. Each widget can turn it off on its own.
